questions.stem: According to the passage, what made the use of newly opened accounts rise?
options: Enrolment drives that opened more accounts
Direct transfer of wages, subsidies and pensions into the accounts
Lower interest rates on small loans
Free mobile phones for account holders
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says usage rose only when wages, subsidies and pensions began to flow into the accounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the third wave of financial inclusion mentioned in the passage?
options: Digital public infrastructure of accounts, identity and payments
questions.explanation: The third wave rests on digital public infrastructure: accounts, biometric identity and interoperable payments.

questions.stem: What does the author see as the main condition for using payment data to extend credit?
options: The borrower's consent and control over how the data are shared
A government guarantee on all loans
Paper records must also be kept
questions.explanation: The data help only if consent is respected and the borrower controls how the data are shared.

questions.stem: Which word is most similar in meaning to DORMANT as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: Dormant accounts are accounts that are not being used: inactive.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Financial inclusion is complete once accounts are opened
Access to an account alone does not ensure that it is used
Digital data can fully replace collateral
Consumer protection slows inclusion and should be relaxed
questions.explanation: Access is not the same as use: accounts stayed dormant until money began to flow into them.

questions.stem: What is the gross NPA ratio (gross NPA as a percentage of advances) of Bank B?
Which bank has the highest credit-deposit ratio?
The total advances of the four banks are approximately what percentage of their total deposits?
By what percentage is the gross NPA of Bank D more than that of Bank A?
What was the value of the bank's gold loans at the start of the year?
questions.explanation: Gold loans are the remaining 10% of Rs 1,200 crore = Rs 120 crore.

questions.stem: What is the size of the loan book at the end of the year?
questions.explanation: Microfinance grows from 540 to 648 (+108), so the book is 1,200 + 108 = Rs 1,308 crore.

questions.stem: At the end of the year, microfinance makes up approximately what share of the loan book?
In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.explanation: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934; it was nationalised in 1949.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development in India?
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up in 1982 as the apex body for agriculture and rural credit.

questions.stem: How many persons work between S and Q?
questions.explanation: P and R work on floors 2 and 3.
Q works on floor 4, just below T on floor 5.
